source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Weed control is important work in growing corn because weeds compete with corn for nutrients. If left unchecked, weeds can be a major source of competition, robbing the crop of the nutrients it needs, so weeding should be planned according to the corn's growth stages. Before applying top-dress fertilizer at each stage, the corn field should be weeded first.

Weeding schedule -- the source recommends weeding in two rounds:

Round 1: weeded within a window of about 15 to 40 days after planting; this round should be timed to fertilizer top-dressing about 15 to 25 days after planting; weeding should be done when soil moisture is about 30 to 50%, so that it is not too hard to work with a hoe.

Round 2: weeded when it has been about 20 to 25 days since the first weeding; the second weeding should coincide with the timing of the second top-dress fertilizer application to make good use of the disturbed/cleared soil surface for fertilizer uptake.
